neutral_facts.value: The accused, along with five others, approached the victim's house. The accused attacked the victim with an axe, and others caught hold of him. The victim's mother tried to save him and sustained injuries. One of the accused fired a gunshot at the victim, which hit his back, causing fatal injuries. The victim ran out of the courtyard and was later found dead. The post-mortem report indicated a single gunshot wound to the back. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and recovered weapons. The trial court convicted the accused based on the evidence, and the High Court affirmed the conviction.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellants shared the common intention to commit the murder of the deceased, and that the presence of appellant No.2 was established by consistent evidence of the eye-witnesses, who also confirmed that he was armed with a rifle and thus shared the common intention acting in concert with appellant No.1.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no clear evidence of prior concert or meeting of mind before the commission of the offence, and that the deposition of the eye-witnesses were inconsistent and contradictory, which led to the trial court erred in basing the conviction upon such inconsistent evidence.

quotes.text: the High Court erred in affirming the conviction of the appellant No.2-Balaram by invoking Section 34 IPC

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that to invoke Section 34 IPC, it must be established that the criminal act was done by more than one person in furtherance of common intention of all, and that there was common intention on the part of several persons to commit a particular crime, and that the crime was actually committed by them in furtherance of that common intention.

quotes.text: To invoke Section 34 IPC, it must be established that the criminal act was done by more than one person in furtherance of common intention of all

it must be provided that (i) there was common intention on the part of several persons to commit a particular crime; and (ii) in furtherance of that common intention, the crime was actually committed by them

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the High Court affirmed the conviction under Section 302 IPC read with Section 34 IPC, and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment.
